findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched away
findings.body: The test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches the attribute on the `time` module for the whole process. The later `time.sleep(0.1)` (added to 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change') therefore does nothing. The test then immediately calls `step.join()`, which sets the flusher's `stopped` flag. The flusher thread reads `current_drift` only at the top of its loop, so if it is mid-iteration (e.g. inside a Redis round-trip) when the drift is set, it will see `stopped` before ever flushing with the advanced clock and exit without producing anything, leaving `messages` empty. The intended delay needs to use an unpatched sleep (e.g. `from time import sleep` imported before patching, or a dedicated event/condition) or the test will be flaky.

findings.title: Aggregated shard_tag metric tags create huge tag values and unbounded cardinality on rebalance
findings.body: `SpanFlusher.main` builds `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and attaches it to `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`. With the shipped default (`--flusher-processes` default 1), a single flusher process owns *all* assigned shards, so the tag value becomes a comma-joined list of every partition index (potentially dozens), which is unusable for grouping. Worse, the shard set assigned to a consumer changes on every Kafka rebalance, so each rebalance produces a brand-new tag value, creating unbounded time-series cardinality in the metrics backend. Tagging per shard individually (as `flusher_unhealthy` does) or not tagging these timers when multiple shards share a process would avoid this.

findings.title: wait_produce timer uses tag key "shards" while sibling metrics use "shard"
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural) while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` in the same loop use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` (singular). Any dashboard or query grouping flusher metrics by the `shard` tag will silently miss the wait_produce series. The tag key should be `shard` for consistency.

findings.title: get_memory_info() is queried once per shard buffer but memory info is cluster-level
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the Redis memory check now loops over `self.buffers` (one SpansBuffer per flusher process) and calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` on each, summing the results. `get_memory_info()` reports memory for the Redis cluster/nodes, not for the logical shards the buffer is constructed with — all shard buffers point at the same Redis. With N flusher processes this issues N identical INFO queries (potentially to every cluster node) on every submit, instead of the single query the old code made. One call on any single buffer (or caching the result) would be sufficient.

findings.title: Restart of a hung worker cannot kill thread-mode workers, leaking threads and duplicating production
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is deemed hung (`cause == "hang"`), the code only calls `process.kill()` if it is a `multiprocessing.Process`. When `produce_to_pipe` is set (the thread mode used by all tests and any embedded usage), the hung `threading.Thread` cannot be killed and is simply leaked while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement thread with a fresh `SpansBuffer` for the same shards. Both the hung thread and the new thread then run concurrently against the same shard keys and the same `produce_to_pipe`, which can produce duplicate or interleaved segment messages and makes the restart counter meaningless in this mode. At minimum, thread mode should skip or assert on the hang-restart path rather than spawning overlapping workers.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard` (lines 127-132) is never called anywhere in the codebase or tests; restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive` -> `_create_process_for_shards` directly. It should be removed to avoid confusion about which restart path is authoritative.

findings.title: No test exercises the multiprocess (spawn) flusher path introduced by this PR
findings.body: The core change of this PR — spawning real `multiprocessing` processes with per-shard `SpansBuffer` instances, pickling them via `run_with_initialized_sentry`, and restarting crashed/hung processes — is only ever exercised through the `produce_to_pipe` code path, which forces `threading.Thread` instead of a spawned process. The new `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts dictionary lengths (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`), never submits a message, and never verifies that shards sharing a process are actually flushed or that the `_ensure_processes_alive` restart logic works with multiple workers. The production configuration (spawn processes, Kafka producer, shard-to-process round-robin actually flushing segments end-to-end) has zero coverage.
